newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 97 barangays (villages) in Pangasinan, home province of President Fidel Ramos, have passed resolutions calling for a Constitutional amendment that would extend the terms of elected officials by two years. Ramos' term ends in 1998. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- President Fidel Ramos issued an executive order creating the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development which is expected to guarantee peace and progress in Mindanao (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- A second national summit on water will be held on October 15 to ensure steady water supply in the country in the next century (JOURNAL)
- President Fidel Ramos said he was leaving to proponents of constitutional changes to "pursue their initiatives" but stressed this should exclude any plan to extend his term. (THE MANILA TIMES)
- Not a single bid was submitted in Wednesday's auction for a 20 percent stake in the National Steeel Co. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Domestic prices of diesel and liquidifed petroleum gas are expected to rise again by October 12 due to rising demand in the United States and Europe, industry officials said. Philippine oil prices are based on Singapore posted prices. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- Philippine exports in the first eight months of the year increased to $13.03 billion from the year-ago $11.2 billion, the National Statistics Office said. (TODAY)
